thread:
maria: heads-up — after the kernel-arbiter refactor in canary, we're seeing more OOM aborts in prod microbatches. low-volume but reproducible. p95 latency also crept +12%.
jon: ugh. any clear signal whether it's batching or KV cache pressure?
sam: quick summary from the profiler:
```
- avg batch tokens: 48 -> 52
- p95 batch tokens: 110 -> 137
- kv cache resident: 12.4GB -> 13.8GB (on 16GB GPUs)
- kernel choice flip: native-cuda -> optimized-slice in ~23% of traces
- p95 latency: 120ms -> 135ms
- OOMs: 3/day -> ~18/day (small spike windows)
```
devon: looks like two things: batch formation is letting fatter batches through when kernel selection switches to optimized-slice (higher temp memory). and KV resident bump pushes memory over watermark.
maria: agreed. hypothesize that the arbiter's kernel switching isn't taking KV headroom into account. it's just using token heuristics.
jon: what if we add a "token pocket" — reserve a small memory cushion per GPU that the batcher uses to limit admission when kv_resident > X? basically a soft cap that lowers max_batch_tokens.
sam: i prototyped something like that locally. config knobs: token_pocket_bytes, pocket_saturation_threshold. when kv_resident > threshold, max_batch_tokens := floor((gpu_free_bytes - token_pocket_bytes) / avg_token_mem).
devon: nice. that ties admission to actual memory. also need to surface kernel memory delta: some kernels need extra scratch. if arbiter can attach kernel_mem_delta to decisions, batcher can subtract that from free_bytes.
maria: can we get bench-bot to collect kernel_mem_delta distribution for optimized-slice vs native-cuda for the canary traffic?
bench-bot: collecting kernel delta histograms now — ETA ~5m.
jon: also we should avoid a hard drop in throughput. propose a staged policy:
- nominal: token_pocket_bytes = 600MB, threshold = 75% kv_utilization
- degrade: pocket = 1.2GB, threshold = 60%
- emergency: pocket = 2GB, threshold = 50% + reject low-priority requests
this keeps latency SLOs while preventing OOMs.
sam: added a microbatch_coalescer change too: prefer more smaller batches when kernel_mem_delta high. reduces peak scratch at the cost of throughput. need numbers.
bench-bot: kernel_mem_delta histograms ready:
```
optimized-slice: median=420MB p95=820MB
native-cuda: median=120MB p95=220MB
```
bench-bot: current kv_resident windows where OOMs fired: 13.5-14.5GB on 16GB GPUs.
devon: that matches. if optimized-slice can add ~800MB, plus kv bump, we hit >16GB.
maria: plan: 1) push patch to batcher to read kernel_mem_delta from arbiter decisions and compute soft-admission with token_pocket. 2) run an A/B canary on 5% of nodes with pocket=800MB and microbatch_coalescer enabled. 3) monitor OOM count, p95 latency, and tokens_per_sec.
jon: quick thought — we should also add a small hysteresis window to avoid flip-flopping as kv_resident oscillates. maybe 30s hold.
sam: implemented hysteresis in local patch. default hold=45s.
devon: also add a lightweight metric: batch_decision_reject_reason (memory_cushion/kernel_delta/throughput_limit). helps SRE triage.
maria: agree. add telemetry and a rollout playbook: rollback if p95 latency > +20% or OOMs increase.
sam: i'll open the PR with tests + a perf harness simulating kernel deltas and KV growth. PR -> #9856
jon: can we also add a small schedule to check whether retraining the arbiter cost model reduces kernel flips? might be a longer-term fix.
maria: yep, create an issue for arbiter tuning. short-term we do soft-admission. long-term we want arbiter to be memory-aware.
infra-bot: canary build queued (canary-batcher-2026.03.18.1). patch author: sam.
bench-bot: starting A/B run on 5% of canary nodes; will report hourly.
jon: thanks all. if the canary looks good, roll to 30% and we can tune pocket sizes.
maria: logging action items:
- sam: PR + perf harness (#9856)
- devon: add reject_reason metric + dashboard
- jon: canary rollout steps + playbook
- bench-bot: hourly report (OOMs/p95/tokens_per_sec)
- infra-bot: watch for any crashloop alerts

maria: quick note — keep an eye on tail p999s too; small user-facing spikes were reported.
devon: noted. I'll add p999 to the dashboard lines.
jon: if anyone sees >5 OOMs/hour from canary, pause rollout.
sam: pushing PR in ~10m. will ping here when green. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: canary build started on nodes [gpu-c05,gpu-c09,gpu-c12].
